procedural_history.impugned_order: Order dated 18.01.2018 passed by the Trial Court rejecting the prosecution's application under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. to recall M. Krishna (PW-189) and produce a report and certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The State filed Criminal Petition No. 2585 of 2019 in the High Court of Karnataka at Bengaluru challenging the Trial Court's order. The High Court, vide order dated 27.01.2022, upheld the Trial Court's order.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The State appealed to the Supreme Court (Criminal Appeal No. 3456 of 2023) against the High Court's order. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the orders of the courts below, and allowed the prosecution's application under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C.

directions: The orders passed by the courts below are set aside.
Application filed by the prosecution under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.
The Trial Court shall proceed with the matter further.

issue.issue_text: Whether the application filed by the prosecution under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. for recalling a witness (PW-189) and producing a certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act, 1872, was rightly rejected by the lower courts on the ground of delay.

facts: The prosecution filed an application under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. to recall a witness (PW-189) and produce a certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act.
This was done after the Trial Court, on 07.04.2017, refused to admit a CFSL report into evidence because it lacked the required Section 65B certificate.
The prosecution then obtained the certificate on 27.04.2017 and sought to introduce it.
The Trial Court and the High Court rejected this application, primarily on the ground that there was a delay of six years in producing the certificate.
law: Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. grants courts the power to recall a witness at any stage if their evidence is essential for a just decision.
A certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act is a procedural requirement to prove the authenticity of an electronic record already on file; it is not new evidence created after the fact.
Allowing the prosecution to file evidence at a later stage is permissible if it does not cause serious or irreversible prejudice to the accused, who must be given a full opportunity to rebut it.
application: The Supreme Court found that the lower courts' reasoning of a six-year delay was based on a "wrong premise."

The Court clarified that there was no actual delay, as the need for the certificate only arose when the Trial Court objected to the report's admissibility on 07.04.2017. The prosecution acted promptly after this objection while the trial was still pending.
The Court reasoned that allowing the certificate would not cause any "irreversible prejudice" to the accused, as they would have a full opportunity to challenge and rebut this evidence.
It was held that denying the prosecution the opportunity to produce the certificate, which is a legal requirement to prove an existing report, would cause a "great injustice."
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the lower courts were wrong to reject the prosecution's application on the ground of delay. It held that there was no culpable delay, and allowing the production of the Section 65B certificate was essential for justice and would not unfairly prejudice the accused.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the application filed by the prosecution under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. for recalling a witness (PW-189) and producing a certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act, 1872, was rightly rejected by the lower courts on the ground of delay.
appellant_arguments: The evidence sought to be produced was not newly created but was merely a certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act for primary evidence (electronic devices and a CFSL report) that was already on record.
The application was filed only after the accused raised an objection to the production of the report, and the prosecution wanted to ensure its admissibility.
Given the serious nature of the case, which involved serial bomb blasts that shocked the country, the lower courts should have considered the application in that light.
There was no delay, as the application was filed immediately after the court rejected the initial attempt to produce the report.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution cannot be allowed to fill a lacuna in its evidence by filing an application under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C.
The certificate was sought to be produced after a delay of six years, and therefore, the lower courts rightly rejected the application.
Allowing the application at this late stage would cause great prejudice to the respondents and would deprive them of their right to a fair trial.

cases.principle: A certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 is a mandatory pre-requisite for the admissibility of electronic records as evidence.

cases.case_name: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
cases.principle: A certificate required under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 can be produced at any stage of the trial.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A certificate required under Section 65-B of the Indian Evidence Act can be produced at any stage of the trial, so long as the hearing is not yet over. The court may permit the production of such a certificate at a later stage, provided it conducts a balancing exercise to ensure that doing so does not cause serious or irreversible prejudice to the accused.
obiter: The exercise of power by the courts in criminal trials to permit evidence to be filed at a later stage should be for the cause of justice, public interest, and to uphold the truth.
If the accused desires to produce the requisite certificate as part of the defence, the court's discretion will depend upon the justice of the case.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court concluded that the certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act is not new evidence, but rather a procedural requirement to prove a report that is already on record. Allowing the prosecution to produce this certificate, even at a later stage, does not cause irreversible prejudice to the accused, as they will have a full opportunity to rebut the evidence. The lower courts erred by rejecting the application on the grounds of delay, as the exercise of power under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. is necessary in this case to uphold the truth and serve the cause of justice.
legal_tests_applied: The power under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C. can be exercised to subserve the cause of justice and public interest, and to uphold the truth.
A fair trial in a criminal case means that no guilty person should go scot-free and no innocent person should be punished; it is not about being fair to only one of the parties.
An application to produce evidence should be allowed if it does not result in any irreversible prejudice to the accused, who must have a full opportunity to rebut it.
policy_considerations: The object of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to arrive at the truth.
Fair trial in a criminal case does not mean that it should be fair to one of the parties. Rather, the object is that no guilty should go scot-free and no innocent should be punished.
Denying the prosecution an opportunity to produce a required certificate under Section 65-B of the Act would cause great injustice to the State.
